input.question: KRaft timeout-metrics design discussion: should fetch/election timeout count metrics always report a value or register/unregister based on node state?

content.content: {"result":"{\"answer\":\"The final consensus was to always report the fetch/election timeout count metrics, not register/unregister them based on node state.\\n\\nSupporting facts in time order:\\n- 2026-04-21T17:32:24.000000Z: Tony Tang started the KIP-1322 discussion on adding metrics to KRaft to measure timeout counts [mail:1a3f3691f5f66b0140de7cb2].\\n- 2026-04-30T20:03:26.000000Z: Kevin Wu agreed that having metrics for timeouts in KRaft would be a nice addition [mail:de13bee9f8bb79338315e881].\\n- 2026-05-01T22:12:17.000000Z: Kevin Wu initially argued (KW3) that count metrics should not report values when the objects they are associated with do not exist, and proposed keeping the internal counter across state transitions while only registering/unregistering the metric based on whether the underlying timer exists [mail:f6b22d1fd37806fcb2175ac0].\\n- 2026-05-04T16:24:01.000000Z: Tony Tang agreed with Kevin Wu's initial approach: keep the internal counter across state transitions, but only register/unregister the metric based on whether the underlying timer exists [mail:fe09c09ac5ddd78f3011c191].\\n- 2026-05-13: Kevin Wu reversed his position, noting that downstream observability platforms may not capture values well if metrics are unregistered during intermittent states (Prospective, Candidate, etc.), and concluded it is fine to always report these metrics [mail:aa4a89deddc8b16336616ab2].\\n- 2026-05-14: Tony Tang agreed, noting that if the election timeout metric were only registered during Unattached/Prospective/Candidate (short states), operators might never see it since nodes spend most time in Follower or Leader [mail:db399df8a2e4d63cd49faeb4].\\n- 2026-05-14: Both confirmed the final consensus: always report the metrics (not register/unregister based on node state), and increment the counter only when the corresponding timer goes from unexpired to expired during a poll of the raft client [mail:8ea2d404f2c259c3934f9386][mail:0f2639ff8155c501d54c3ee4].\\n\\nWhat could not be determined: Nothing; the findings fully answer the
